records.title: Transverse marked context coverages generate Grothendieck topologies
records.statement: On the powerset poset L=P({0,1}x{0,1}), the ACBE and RPM coordinate-partition families, together with the null cover of the empty context, are pullback-stable bases whose generated sieves define Grothendieck topologies J_A and J_R. Parallel immutable mark records preserve cover kind, source authority, evidence references, and pullback ancestry even when the generated unmarked families coincide.
assumptions: Arrows in L are inclusions
Pullbacks are intersections
Each marked family at V is {V intersect B_0 -> V, V intersect B_1 -> V}
The empty family covers the empty context
records.claim_boundary: The topology theorem is mathematical; the hash-stable provenance behavior is an executable serialization invariant. Neither is evidence that either marking measures an empirical property.

records.title: Neither marked global generator contains an identity
records.statement: At the four-atom global context, both pieces of the ACBE generator and both pieces of the RPM generator are proper subcontexts. Their generated sieves are nonmaximal.
assumptions: The context contains all four atoms
Both coordinate blocks are nonempty and proper
records.claim_boundary: Nonmaximality repairs the inherited formal collapse; it does not establish semantic correctness of the labels.

records.title: The two marked context topologies are subcanonical
records.statement: Every representable presheaf on L satisfies the ACBE and RPM generating-cover sheaf conditions, so both generated topologies on the context factor are subcanonical.
object_types: Generated context topologies J_A and J_R
assumptions: Representables are evaluated on the inclusion poset
Each marked cover is jointly exhaustive by union
records.claim_boundary: This applies to the context factor L only. It does not make the inherited jointly-surjective topology on Noetica subcanonical.

records.title: ACBE and RPM sheafification modalities are distinct and non-identity
records.statement: There is an explicit finite presheaf F_A that is a J_A-sheaf but not a J_R-sheaf, and a symmetric F_R that is a J_R-sheaf but not a J_A-sheaf. Therefore the two reflective sheaf subcategories and their sheafification modalities are distinct on PSh(L). External product with a representable yC_0 lifts the witnesses to the ambient successor topos PSh(C x L), so neither ambient modality is the identity.
object_types: Ambient presheaf topos PSh(C x L)
assumptions: F_A assigns a bit to every complete ACBE block contained in a context
F_R is defined symmetrically for RPM blocks
records.claim_boundary: No commutation or noncommutation claim is made in this version.

records.title: The marked modalities restrict to identity on the joined resolved subtopos
records.statement: Every object sheaf for J_A join J_R is separately a J_A-sheaf and a J_R-sheaf. Consequently both sheafification reflectors restrict to identity on the fully resolved subtopos E_res; their proved nontriviality applies to the ambient presheaf topos.
assumptions: E_res is the sheaf subcategory for a topology finer than both J_A and J_R
Sheafification is the reflector onto its sheaf subcategory
records.claim_boundary: The successor is a structured ambient modal package with a resolved subtopos; it is not the resolved subtopos mislabeled as carrying nontrivial ACBE/RPM modalities.

records.title: The join of the two context topologies resolves all four atoms
records.statement: The common refinement of the ACBE and RPM partitions is the four-singleton partition. Consequently their joined coverage enforces ordinary gluing over the four atomic contexts; on the finite context factor it generates the union topology.
assumptions: ACBE partitions by the first coordinate
RPM partitions by the second coordinate
records.claim_boundary: This is a structural gluing result for Set-valued context data, not a probabilistic marginal-extension theorem.

records.title: Legacy-to-v2 product-site round trip
records.statement: For E=Sh(Noetica,J_legacy), the proposed product-site comparison is intended to identify the resolved subtopos E_res with four marked E channels. A legacy object is placed in a designated neutral channel and terminal objects in the other channels; categorical evaluation at the neutral channel must yield a specified natural isomorphism ev_00 o iota ~= Id_E, while the separate canonical serialization must preserve registered identifiers and hashes by strict equality.
assumptions: The product-site comparison equivalence is established
A neutral context atom is fixed in the release registry
Bare legacy site objects are sheafified before marking when J_legacy is not subcanonical
records.claim_boundary: Backward compatibility remains a Gate 1 proof and implementation obligation, not a completed theorem. If proved, the resolved context factor is four independent legacy channels and does not by itself provide cross-channel semantics.

records.title: Composition law for ACBE and RPM modalities
records.statement: On the exact finite context presheaf category PSh(L,Set), the explicit ACBE and RPM associated-sheaf reflectors commute up to a unit-compatible canonical natural isomorphism, and either composite is naturally isomorphic to sheafification for the joined atomic topology: M_A M_R ~= M_atom ~= M_R M_A and J_atom = J_A join J_R.
assumptions: L is the powerset inclusion category on four atoms
ACBE and RPM are the stated transverse two-block partitions
The null family covers the empty context
Presheaves and sheaves are ordinary small Set-valued functors in a fixed universe
records.claim_boundary: This theorem is scoped to PSh(L,Set). The lift to PSh(C x L), coherence in the C coordinate, interaction with observational covers, proof-assistant verification, and independent category-theory review remain OPEN.
